scope: Source-only feasibility gate for unaccepted DRM supervisor; no tracing, ptrace, ioctl, native run, build, dependency adoption or system tuning.
status: Current GEM_BUSY-to-final-fdinfo rule is insufficient; do not spend proposed conformance/calibration runs on this draft.

host.limitation: Read-only identity only. Upstream v6.12.107 files are pinned feasibility sources, not proof of exact Debian module equivalence or active submission backend. Sysfs enable_guc was unreadable without privilege; no elevation attempted.

chain.finding: Busy uses request signaled/HW sequence completion, and ignores foreign fences. It does not invoke an engine-accounting retirement barrier.

Fdinfo sums past_runtime and runtime of contexts still on ctx_list. Runtime uses accumulated values plus active estimate, with optional backend update_stats. It does not itself wait for stale engine retirement.

Context close replaces engines with NULL and removes ctx_list membership. Engine release can await active schedule-out/retirement asynchronously; its FENCE_COMPLETE callback transfers runtime to past_runtime. Context destroy returns after context_close, without an explicit wait for this accounting callback.

Execlists updates accumulated hardware runtime at context status processing/schedule-out. Its inspected ops table has no update_stats callback. Hardware sequence completion therefore is not the same observed condition as that accounting update.

The active barrier registers a wait-queue callback and increments pending completion. Software fence commit releases its initial pending count; it is not a synchronous wait for all registered completions. This corroborates the possible deferred accounting transfer. The subsequent kill_context path brackets kill_engines with pending-count await/complete operations, not the separate synchronous i915_sw_fence_wait primitive. It does not establish the missing accounting-finalization postcondition.

scenario: A workload request reaches HW completion while context schedule-out/retirement processing remains pending.
GEM_BUSY can report idle from request completion.
Explicit context destruction removes the context from current fdinfo enumeration; pending retirement has not yet transferred its runtime to past_runtime.
Reading fdinfo at this point can miss that pending accounting. Retaining a duplicate DRM file preserves the file/client, not an independently destroyed context in the enumerated context list.
inference.strength: Source-supported allowed interleaving in inspected upstream code, not a reproduced event or an assertion that every host read is incomplete. It is enough to reject busy-idle as the proposed completeness proof.
inference.not_claimed: No hardware infeasibility, Wayland defect, renderer cause, observed counter loss, or impossibility of another complete observer.

disposition: The unaccepted draft must not be promoted unchanged. No new observer execution packet yet.

Before any conformance run, identify a source-backed observable accounting-finalization barrier covering explicit context/engine replacement and destruction as well as every submitted object. A final fence or GEM_BUSY idle alone is insufficient for the demonstrated distinction.
Do not use repeated equal samples/quiet time as proof. Do not drain or hold clients in ways that dilute the active-window denominator or silently change lifetime behavior.

An alternative kernel accounting/event mechanism would require its exact privilege, coverage, loss/retirement semantics and overhead scope separately proposed and owner approved. No such implementation is selected here.
Continue the independently scoped renderer repair. Complete DRM duty remains unavailable and blocks final qualification; the separately proposed crosshair replay can diagnose correctness without it.
remaining: Other DRM-METHOD-01/02/04/05/06 findings remain open. Exact Debian source/config reconciliation and all native observer conformance/calibration remain unperformed.

independent_review.disposition: Source chain corroborated, no logical blocker; advisory only, no execution authority.
